messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated p99 on streaming API (service=inference-service, region=us-west). Automatic incident thread created. :rotating_light:

oncall-bot: Paging sam (oncall) for incidents/streaming-p99-prefetch.

sam: I have the page. pulling graphs now. p99 ~ 1.9s, p95 ~ 460ms, p50 stable. Seeing a sharp drop in prefix cache hit-rate.

miguel: confirmed. spike coincides with today's Canary rollout: inference-service@hashseed-rotate-2026-03-15 (10:25 UTC). Canary receives 20% traffic.

sam: what changed in the rollout?

miguel: small change: seed rotation for prefix hashing to reduce hotspotting. The code path modified how prefix -> cache_key is computed (seed appended before murmurhash).

sam: any errors or 5xx?

infra-bot: Metrics snapshot: prefix_cache_hit_rate: 92% -> 12% within 45s of canary. downstream CPU increased, queueing latency up. No 5xx spike, but streaming partial-close events increased by ~0.8%.

ana: CS inbound: 2 customers reported truncated streams and increased latency on streaming endpoints. I'm on standby to coordinate.

sam: immediate risks: long tail latency, customer retries. mitigation options: 1) rollback canary, 2) roll-forward with compatibility shim (try new key, then old key), 3) aggressive prefetch of top prefixes into canary pods, 4) divert traffic to stable nodes. Thoughts?

miguel: compatibility shim might avoid full rollback but needs a quick code push and rollout — risky during live spike. Prefetch is safer and fast.

sam: preferring fast rollback to stable, then plan compatibility shim. Rolling back canary now.

sam: command: ```bash
kubectl -n prod rollout undo deploy/inference-service --to-revision=stable-2026-03-14
```

infra-bot: Rolling back canary: new pods terminating; stable pods scaling to replace. Health checks in progress.

sam: while rollback proceeds, kick off prefetch to warm caches on newly created pods so they don't suffer cold start. script: ```bash
python ops/prefetch.py --mode top-prefixes --count 1000 --qps 30
```

miguel: starting prefetch against stable pool only. Using low concurrency to avoid overload.

20s later...

infra-bot: Rollback completed successfully. New replica set at stable-2026-03-14 in service. Pod health OK.

sam: watching telemetry. p99 -> 380ms within 90s of rollback. prefix_hit_rate recovering to ~88%. Great.

ana: customers reporting improvement. Rachel (CS) asking for a short post-incident summary for affected accounts.

rachel: noted. I'll prepare outreach and bundle logs. Please add exact spike window and estimated impact per account.

miguel: root cause analysis (initial): hash seed rotation changed the hash output for existing prefixes with no migration path. Cache keys mismatched, effectively causing a large-scale cache cold start. This increased compute work and introduced queueing/tail latency.

sam: immediate action items (done): rollback canary, prefetch top prefixes, set incident severity to Sev2.

sam: follow-ups (short-term):
- Add an automated canary-safety gate: if prefix_cache_hit_rate delta > 30% within 2m, auto-halt rollout.
- Add synthetic preflight: run a simulated cache-compatibility check against representative keyspace before rollout.
- Create an alert rule for simultaneous p99 > 1.0s and cache-hit drop > 40% during rollouts.

miguel: follow-ups (long-term):
- Implement key-versioning in cache layer so servers accept both v1 and v2 keys for a configurable overlap window.
- Build a small compatibility library that can be toggled at runtime to do dual-lookup (try new key, fallback to old).
- Add canary workload generator that exercises prefix-cache distribution and reports hit-rate degradation before traffic ramp.

sam: I'll open RFC for key-versioning and timeline; Miguel will own implementation.

miguel: creating INF ticket INF-4901 for key-versioning + CI preflight work.

rachel: CS impact: two customers had elevated retry rates and one experienced ~90s of degraded streaming (user-facing lag). Notifying AEs and offering to run a joint postmortem call if requested.

sam: estimate: incident active window ~10:25:40 -> 10:28:20 UTC. Peak p99 at 10:26:10 UTC.

ana: can we confirm whether this affected embeddings endpoints or only streaming?

miguel: primarily streaming and any endpoint using prefix cache. Embeddings service uses a different cache key scheme, unaffected.

sam: audit checklist:
- tag the deploy as rolled-back in release notes.
- attach timeline and metric snapshots to incident doc.
- run postmortem with root cause, mitigations, and customer impact summaries.

infra-bot: Autoscaler scaled stable pods +4 during mitigation and then stabilized. No resource exhaustion.

sam: Decision: no SLA credits yet; CS to evaluate based on account impact.

rachel: will follow up with affected accounts; will recommend credits if they escalate.

miguel: additional recommendation: for future seed rotations, generate a migration map for hottest prefixes and pre-populate new keys ahead of rollout.

sam: assigning postmortem owner: miguel. He'll draft, I'll review. Miguel please include timelines, chart links, and the preflight test plan.

miguel: acknowledged. will publish draft within 2 hours and schedule RCA meeting.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated. handoff to oncall for watch.

oncall-bot: handoff: sam -> ana (overnight watch). Ana is acknowledged. Watch window until 2523007777.

ana: taking watch. I'll check hit-rate every 15m for the next 6 hours and pause any rollouts until the key-versioning plan is in place.

sam: thanks everyone. closing live thread; postmortem to follow. :white_check_mark:
